title: Signature Convergence Certificates
description: Signature edition: after replicas sync, the workspace issues a convergence certificate — a signed statement that all known replicas hold the identical document hash. Auditors can verify collaboration converged without inspecting every replica. This is a Signature original method.
method: Replicas exchange state hashes via the sync channel; when all match, a quorum signs the certificate binding (document id, hash, replica set, timestamp).
usage: Issue certificates at sync milestones; require them before archival snapshots.

demo.code:
import hashlib
h = hashlib.sha256(b'doc-v42').hexdigest()[:10]
print(f'converged: all 3 replicas hold {h} -> certificate signed')

title: Signature Operational transformation (OT)
description: Signature edition: Operational transformation, the algorithm behind Google Docs' original collaboration, transforms concurrent operations against each other so they apply cleanly in any order. A central server (or equivalent ordering) serializes ops; clients transform their pending ops against incoming ones — convergence through transformation functions.
method: Server orders ops; clients transform local pending ops against remote ops (transform function per op pair); all replicas apply the same total order.
usage: Use when a central server is acceptable; implement transform functions carefully — they're the correctness core.

demo.code:
print('OT: A inserts "x" at 0; B inserts "y" at 0 concurrently')
print('transform: B\'s insert shifts to position 1 -> both converge on "xy"')

title: Signature Tombstone-free deletion (OR-Sets)
description: Signature edition: Naive CRDT deletion needs tombstones (remembering what was deleted) forever. Observed-Remove Sets avoid permanent tombstones: each add carries a unique tag, and remove only cancels observed tags — unobserved concurrent adds survive, and garbage collection can eventually drop old state safely.
method: Add = (element, unique tag); remove = cancel known tags; merge unions adds and cancels; GC drops fully-removed elements after causality is stable.
usage: Prefer OR-Sets for collaborative collections; run causal-stability GC to bound growth.

title: Signature Fractional indexing for ordering
description: Signature edition: When collaborators reorder items concurrently, fractional indexing assigns each item a position key between its neighbors (a0, a1, a0V...) so inserts never renumber the whole list. Order merges deterministically across replicas — the trick behind Figma-like canvas ordering and collaborative lists.
method: Keys are variable-length strings ordered lexicographically; insert between neighbors by generating a midpoint key; rebalance rarely when keys grow long.
usage: Use for any collaboratively-ordered list; rebalance keys in the background when they get long.

demo.code:
keys = ['a0', 'a1']
mid = 'a0V'  # between a0 and a1
ordered = sorted(keys + [mid])
print('order after concurrent insert:', ordered)

title: Signature Delta-state synchronization
description: Signature edition: Shipping full CRDT state on every sync wastes bandwidth. Delta-state CRDTs send only what changed since the peer's last known state (tracked via version vectors), making sync proportional to activity, not document size — essential for large collaborative documents on mobile networks.
method: Track per-peer version vectors; compute delta = ops the peer hasn't seen; send deltas; merge; advance the vector.
usage: Implement version vectors per peer; fall back to full-state sync if vectors desynchronize.

demo.code:
vv = {'peerB': 12}
ops = [(i, f'op{i}') for i in range(15)]
delta = [op for i, op in ops if i >= vv['peerB']]
print(f'send delta: {len(delta)} ops (not all 15)')

title: Signature Multi-value conflict display
description: Signature edition: Sometimes convergence shouldn't silently pick a winner: multi-value registers keep all concurrent values and show the conflict in the UI ('Ana wrote X, Ben wrote Y — pick one'). The data structure converges (same set everywhere); the humans resolve the semantics.
method: Concurrent writes accumulate in a set; UI renders all values with authors; user picks; the pick is a new write that supersedes.
usage: Use for fields where silent LWW would lose meaningful disagreement (names, decisions, priorities).

title: Signature Presence and cursor sharing
description: Signature edition: Seeing collaborators' cursors and selections (presence) is separate from document convergence: ephemeral state broadcast over the same sync channel. Presence uses last-writer-wins with heartbeats and expiry — stale cursors fade when a peer disconnects, no locks involved.
method: Broadcast (user, cursor, selection) on change; expire after heartbeat timeout; render remote cursors as decorations; never block editing on presence.
usage: Throttle presence broadcasts; expire aggressively; presence must never gate editing.

title: Signature Automerge JSON documents
description: Signature edition: Automerge brings CRDTs to JSON-like documents: maps, lists, text, and counters that merge automatically across peers. Local-first apps use it so every device holds a full replica, edits work offline, and sync merges without conflicts or a server.
method: Document as op log; changes produce ops; peers exchange and merge op logs; current state is the deterministic fold of all ops.
usage: Use for local-first collaborative apps; sync op logs through any transport; keep the op log compacted.

demo.code:
doc = {'title': 'Plan', 'tasks': ['a']}
remote_ops = [('tasks', 'append', 'b')]
doc['tasks'].append('b')
print('merged doc:', doc, '(op log merged, no conflicts)')

title: Signature Conflict-free task boards
description: Signature edition: Kanban boards are natural CRDTs: cards as OR-Sets (add/remove with unique ids), columns as ordered lists, assignments as LWW registers. Two people dragging the same card concurrently resolve deterministically — last-writer-wins by timestamp, or multi-value for explicit conflict display.
method: Cards in OR-Set; position via fractional indexing; field updates as LWW-Registers with hybrid logical clocks; conflicts surfaced, never lost.
usage: Use fractional indexing for drag-order; show multi-value conflicts in the UI when they occur.

demo.code:
board = {'todo': ['card1'], 'doing': []}
# two users move card1 concurrently -> LWW by hybrid clock
board['todo'].remove('card1'); board['doing'].append('card1')
print('resolved board:', board)
